title: The price that spiked 400 percent
blurb: Concurrent updates each passed their own guardrail check.
prompt: A product's price jumped 400 percent in an hour because ten parallel updates each evaluated against the old price and all passed, and a model timeout froze an experimental price as production. Review it, fix it, and prove headroom is shared and sources are honest.
aiNote: The draft evaluates each update against the on-disk price in isolation, so N concurrent updates each within the per-update limit compound far past the intended per-window cap, and on a model timeout it serves the last suggestion with a fresh timestamp as if it were newly computed.
testIdea: Fire ten concurrent 15 percent updates and assert the cumulative move respects the 20 percent window bound; time out the model and assert the published price carries the stale marker and last approved value; inspect a storefront response for experiment prices.
followUps: How do you roll back a bad price across storefronts?
What does a reason code need to be auditable?
